<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**8** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **3** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0dc84b02a827384113b64afb06d52ef6ecb0496f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5c13610c65a4410a715654925c1bbdaebea1e7c1` — the merge of head `c9be4172166b42203f4ccb146de37da07be97887` into base `0dc84b02a827384113b64afb06d52ef6ecb0496f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5c13610c65a4410a715654925c1bbdaebea1e7c1 && git checkout 5c13610c65a4410a715654925c1bbdaebea1e7c1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0dc84b02a827384113b64afb06d52ef6ecb0496f c9be4172166b42203f4ccb146de37da07be97887 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0dc84b02a827384113b64afb06d52ef6ecb0496f && git merge --no-ff c9be4172166b42203f4ccb146de37da07be97887

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0dc84b02a827384113b64afb06d52ef6ecb0496f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · 2026-11-11T14:04Z

Head-sha: `c9be4172166b42203f4ccb146de37da07be97887`

- **Shape:** draft → `main`. First line `Fixes #32406`, which should close the card on merge. No other open card number sits beside a closing keyword (whole body scanned). `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are on their own lines in both the body and the changeset.
- **Scope:** 5 files, all inside the claim's surface (`db-job-adapter.ts`, three of its test files, `.changeset/32406-job-run-trigger.md`). Nothing under `content/docs/releases/`, `packages/spec`, `ui/**` or `skills/**`. The changeset bumps `@objectstack/service-job` patch; I checked each sentence against the diff: manual → `manual`, one `replay` row per attempt, handler context unchanged, old rows keep their values. All are true.
- **Premise measured:** the before readings sit in the PR body (7 failed / 2 passed on unmodified 7d82b2da, with `[schedule, schedule]` for `trigger()` and 2 rows for `replay()`), plus the retried-replay disagreement the synthetic row caused.
- **Seat spot reads (`origin/main` 0dc84b02):**
  - `git grep sys_job_run` over non-test `packages/**` and `ui/**`: hits are the CLI ownership inventory (table-name list), the generated translation bundles, and the adapter itself. No reader of the `trigger` value, so the PR body's "no consumer" holds and `Clause-②: no` stands.
  - Diff read: `runTriggerOf` takes the replay claim once and otherwise reads `ctx.trigger ?? 'schedule'`, with the fallback documented as the cron adapter's scheduled fire. `replay()` reads the wrapper after the guard's await, and its synthetic `startRun`/`finishRun` are removed.
- **Pins and ablation:** new describe block covering both assemblies. One ablation (`ctx.trigger ?? 'schedule'` → `'schedule'`) gave 4 red, then restored with blob == HEAD. A reverse check of the guard-race pin went red as expected. A stale pin at the old L302 was corrected as the card asked.
- **Gates:** dev local `dispatch-gates.mjs` 68 families: 65 exit 0 and 3 NOT MEASURED (shallow-clone / whole-repo `dist` prerequisites); `pnpm lint` exit 0. Landing waits on check-runs at this head: Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check `success`, and every other check green or expected-skip.
- **Accepted deviations:** two out-of-date replay pins corrected in sibling test files (read as "its tests"); a new `node:async_hooks` import, with precedent in `@objectstack/core` and `service-automation`; local scope narrowed to the package plus derived gates, the full farm left to CI.
- **Out of scope:** `sys_job_run.attempt`'s description and `jobs.mdx` say a replay's attempt is above 1, but no code writes that, before or after this PR. Doc drift, not made false here → `noted, not filed` (p3 doc nit; filing it would cost more than it is worth). `Skills-docs:` not owed (`Metadata-protocol: none`).
- **Landing:** non-governed paths, 375 changed lines, no Tier H. The seat lands it: `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` once the checks above are green at this head.
